summary: Worked example (live, owner-supervised, 2026-11-28) — the fee-waiver correspondence from the November 2026 grant cycle, captured as a lesson per CONTINUOUS_LEARNING_AND_GROWTH.md. WHAT WAS SENT: three emails from interplanetarysister@gmail.com (the address used on the applications), each requesting a waiver before any payment, per the owner's always-waive rule — (1) Amber Grant: to info@ambergrantsforwomen.com, citing WomensNet's own FAQ waiver route for the $15 fee; (2) IFundWomen Startup Accelerator Grant: to grants@ifundwomen.com, citing Official Rules Section 5, which lets an applicant who cannot afford the $5 fee request a waiver by email — requested BEFORE applying, as the rules require, because an application counts as complete only once payment is received; (3) Hey Helen Grant: to hello@visionaries.co, a polite exception inquiry for the $15 fee that acknowledges the terms describe it as non-refundable while asking whether a hardship process exists. HerSuiteSpot publishes no email, so the HerRise waiver ask went through their official 'Submit Your Question Here' contact form instead. EMAIL CRAFT (the reusable pattern): the subject names the ask and the program ('Fee waiver request — Startup Accelerator Grant'); the opening cites the funder's own waiver route or rule, so the request reads as following their process rather than asking a favour; one short paragraph carries verified business facts only (woman-owned Washington sole proprietorship, registered October 2, 2026, live, pre-revenue, self-funded AI-powered fundraising platform); the deadline is stated plainly (November 30, 2026); the close asks for the process ('please let me know how the waiver is applied'); the signature is Michelle Rogers, Founder, Interplanetary Fund, with the website and city (Everett, Washington). PROCESS LESSONS: (1) pursue the waiver first on every fee — a fee becomes an owner pay-or-skip decision only after the waiver route is exhausted or denied; (2) verify the sending account before sending — the connected Gmail account was a different address (cuddlemeplatonically@gmail.com), so nothing was sent from the wrong account; the sends were routed through the owner's Chrome Gmail session from interplanetarysister@gmail.com and confirmed in that account's Sent folder; (3) when a funder publishes no email, use their official contact form rather than guessing an address; (4) an auto-responder reply (WomensNet answered within a minute) is an acknowledgment, not a decision — the waiver stays outstanding until a substantive reply arrives. APPLICATION: improves GRANT_APPLICATION_PLAYBOOK.md (the waiver step of the grant cycle) and general correspondence practice for future funder and partner email. Filed unverified by design: owner-observed work, not a checked external source.
